title: Run all_done_min_one_success tasks inside mapped task groups
body:
related: #39801, #69377

<!-- HUMAN SUMMARY - AGENTS DO NOT MODIFY -->

<!-- END OF HUMAN SUMMARY -->

<details><summary>AI Summary</summary>

A task with `trigger_rule="all_done_min_one_success"` inside a dynamically mapped task group never expands when all of its direct upstreams are in the same group. Its unexpanded placeholder (`map_index=-1`) is marked `upstream_failed` and the Dag run fails, even when every upstream instance succeeds:

```
init[-1] = success
tg.imsleepy[0..2] = success
tg.imawake[-1] = upstream_failed   # never expands
```

Reproduced with `airflow dags test` in Breeze on main.

**Cause.** For the placeholder, the relevant map index of an in-group upstream is `-1`. Once that upstream expands, no upstream task instance has map index `-1`, so the placeholder counts zero upstreams. `all_success`, `none_failed` and `all_done` pass on zero upstreams and the task expands. `all_done_min_one_success` reads zero as "all done, none succeeded" and sets `upstream_failed`.

**Fix.** When a placeholder inside a mapped task group has no upstream task instance left to judge, the trigger rule check now passes without setting a state. The task expands and each expanded instance evaluates its own upstreams, as with the other "all done" rules.

#69377 fixed the same symptom for `none_failed_min_one_success` by adding it to `is_fast_triggered`. Doing the same here was rejected: the placeholder would then count every upstream instance, so one skipped index would skip the whole task. It would also regress shapes that work on main today, such as a task that also takes the group's mapped argument.

Per-index results for `all_done_min_one_success`, in-group upstream only:

| Upstream index 1 | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| succeeds | `{-1: upstream_failed}` | `{0, 1, 2: success}` |
| skipped | `{-1: upstream_failed}` | `{0: success, 1: skipped, 2: success}` |
| failed | `{-1: upstream_failed}` | `{0: success, 1: upstream_failed, 2: success}` |

Shapes where the task also has the mapped argument or an outside task as upstream already decide per index on main and are unchanged.

A before/after comparison of `dag.test()` runs covered every trigger rule except `always`, several upstream shapes, skipped/failed upstream indexes, branching, zero-length expansion and a mapped group inside a loop. Only `all_done_min_one_success` results changed, and all to per-index states.

Known limitations, not regressions:

- `all_done_min_one_success` with a **failed** upstream outside the group and a successful one inside still ends `{-1: upstream_failed}`, as on main.
- `none_failed_min_one_success` (#69377) still fails the whole task when one in-group upstream index fails. Moving it from `is_fast_triggered` to this guard may fix that; left for a follow-up.

</details>

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("upstream_outcome", "expected_state"),
+    [("skip", "skipped"), ("fail", "upstream_failed")],
+)
+def test_all_done_min_one_success_decides_per_index_in_mapped_task_group(
+    dag_maker, upstream_outcome, expected_state
+):
+    """An ``ALL_DONE_MIN_ONE_SUCCESS`` task in a mapped group is evaluated per expanded index."""
+    with dag_maker(dag_id=f"test_all_done_min_one_success_upstream_{upstream_outcome}") as dag:
+
+        @task
+        def init():
+            return ["seize", "the", "day"]
+
+        @task_group(group_id="tg")
+        def tg(message):
+            @task
+            def imsleepy(message):
+                if message == "the":
+                    if upstream_outcome == "skip":
+                        raise AirflowSkipException
+                    raise ValueError("boom")
+                return message
+
+            @task(trigger_rule=TriggerRule.ALL_DONE_MIN_ONE_SUCCESS)
+            def imawake(message):
+                pass
+
+            imawake(imsleepy(message))
+
+        tg.expand(message=init())
+
+    dr = dag.test()
+
+    states: dict[str, dict[int, str | None]] = defaultdict(dict)
+    for ti in dr.get_task_instances():
+        states[ti.task_id][ti.map_index] = ti.state
+
+    assert states["tg.imawake"] == {0: "success", 1: expected_state, 2: "success"}
+
